body:
# Independent audit of the full-parity forest and saturated calibration

Source: `candidate 47e23345c657e546`, Sections1--3. Full independent read: PASS. The source proves a menu-independent union cover under full occupied source parity, not a Gamma-weighted cover.

## 1. Actual cap and forest audit

Positive own strip coarea gives strict threshold decrease immediately to the right of the active threshold; global threshold monotonicity extends the strict inequality to every larger threshold. Equal threshold at two deepest marks would invoke the same full-normal identity with the same positive S, so both marks coincide. Thus every actual cap strictly misses the mark of every other actual source, and every raw balanced menu's average base tilt strictly exposes its own source among the source bases.

Zero strip coarea on a full-dimensional convex fiber forces the uniform outward smoothing integrand to be identically zero or one: intermediate values on its connected interior would give an open positive-volume strip, and continuity treats the boundary. The strict missed-source margin excludes the identically-one alternative. Consequently each cap misses every other source fiber in its entirety, including its boundary.

The positive sampled base set is midpoint-complete: averaging two positive-dimensional fibers gives a positive-dimensional fiber at every integer midpoint. The distance-halving iteration stays in the finite set P. Its positive distances from conv(I) have a positive minimum, so it reaches conv(I) in finitely many steps. The empty source-hull property then makes that terminal point an actual source. The choice of root is independent of menus. Expanding the dyadic recursion and removing self coefficients yields exactly the stated convex relation. Averaged continuous normals vanish, so the positive average base margin gives pointwise union coverage in every continuous coordinate. Saturation upgrades at least one captured point to a whole captured fiber. No response-weight estimate follows from this alone.

## 2. Exact all-tilt interval audit

The four lower endpoints have successive slopes 1/4,1/4,23/40, and the upper endpoints have slopes 41/20,-1/4,-23/40. They define a genuine convex body with the prescribed fibers.

At Y0=(0,-1/10), the positive cap with a=-9/10 has maximal outside margins -1/20 on both K_-1 and K_1 and at most -61/40 on K_2. They are below the whole smoothing strip when w<1/20. Its own mass is 11/10+w/2. For the negative orientation, the minimum margin on K_-1 is 19/20-a, so a<=19/20 captures all of that fiber. If a>19/20, the minimum margin on K_1 is a-17/20>0, capturing its entire mass 3/2. A sufficiently negative tilt captures exactly K_-1 outside. These observations prove the bound and all minimizing outside selectors, for every real tilt.

At Y1=(1,0), either orientation captures all K_2 if a>=7/40. For a<7/40 the K_0 contribution is at least the ordinary length min(2,1-a)>33/40, greater than 7/20. A sufficiently positive tilt captures exactly K_2 outside for both orientations. The own mass 3/4+w/2 gives the same Q=11/10+w/2. Again every equality tilt has saturated outside fibers.

The pure-base mass bounds 11/5 and 37/20 exceed Q. On each middle fiber, freezing its two active caps shows strict depth decrease for every nonzero motion above or below the displayed mark: the appropriate own cap strictly loses mass before emptying and the outside mass is nonincreasing. The exposed endpoint fibers have depth at most their total masses, both below Q. Hence these are exactly the two deepest marks, with both parities occupied, and all active nonvertical caps have zero outside coarea.

The positive-orientation cap at source0 nevertheless has outside mass zero whereas its pure-base reserve is 1/5. Every balanced menu contains that orientation. Thus saturation and full source parity do not imply a zero-deficit menu. The response weights equal one half because all coarea is on the interval containing the source. The example is correctly paid by the d=1 single-cap hinge mechanism; it obstructs only the stronger deficit claim.

## 3. A quantified addition: the forest coefficient is at most one half

Let z not in I take t>=1 midpoint steps before FIRST reaching p_i. The dyadic expansion is

    p_i=2^(-t)z + sum_{r=0}^{t-1}2^(-(t-r)) p(T^r z).

The final chosen source p(T^(t-1)z), whose coefficient is 1/2, differs from p_i: otherwise the final midpoint equation would force T^(t-1)z=p_i, contrary to first arrival. If c is the total coefficient of p_i in the expansion, the non-self denominator satisfies

    1-c >= 2^(-t)+1/2.

After removing self coefficients, the coefficient lambda of z therefore satisfies

    0<lambda=2^(-t)/(1-c)
       <=1/(1+2^(t-1)) <=1/2.                          (1)

Thus the total ratio of the other-source coefficients to lambda is at least one. This strengthens the bare positivity statement without any geometric classification of full-parity empty lattice polytopes.

## 4. Quantified source-width reserve, and its exact limitation

Normalize each cap in a raw menu by Gamma(u)=1 and the menu by sum rho=1. Put

    P_j = sum_l rho_l h_{K_j-y_j}(u_l)>0.

The strict positivity follows because y_j is in the interior of its fiber and every u_l is nonzero. In the zero-outside-coarea setting the cap misses the whole other source fiber. For the uniform outward width h this means, for each menu cap l,

    a_l·(p_j-p_i)+u_l·(y_j-y_i)+h_{K_j-y_j}(u_l)<=-h.

Average and use sum rho_l u_l=0 to obtain the exact inequality

    a_bar_i·(p_j-p_i)<=-P_j-h.                        (2)

For the forest-root relation

    p_i=lambda z+sum_{j != i}lambda_j p_j,

(2) gives

    a_bar_i·(z-p_i)
       >=sum_{j != i}(lambda_j/lambda)(P_j+h)
       >=h+min_{lambda_j>0} P_j,                     (3)

where the second step uses (1). Thus the average margin at every point of the assigned outside fiber has a definite positive support-width reserve. This retains more actual geometry than the sign-only forest cover.

However (3) still does not bound the RESPONSE weight of captured caps. The positive margins of those caps can vary with the base tilts, and no upper normalization of these margins has been proved. Dividing the reserve by an uncontrolled maximal margin would not give Gamma_d. A numerical payment theorem must supply that missing control, or use the source support functions and fiber volumes by another argument.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
